subject: history_social
passage: In one sixteenth-century European kingdom, laborers were paid in silver coins, and merchants generally priced goods according to the amount of silver a coin actually contained rather than the value stamped on it. Between 1540 and 1560, the crown repeatedly reduced the silver content of its coins, so that by 1560 a coin held less than half the silver it had held in 1540, while the prices of bread and other basic goods, measured in silver, changed little. Historian Margit Lindqvist found that the daily wage recorded for building laborers in the kingdom's capital doubled over the same period. Lindqvist's findings suggest that, compared with laborers in 1540, laborers in 1560 most likely ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: could buy less with a day's wages, even though they received more coins.
choices.B: could buy about twice as much with a day's wages as before.
choices.C: were paid partly in gold to protect them from the loss of silver.
choices.D: earned more than workers in any other part of the kingdom.

explanation.why: Work out the silver in a day's pay. Laborers got twice as many coins, but each coin held less than half as much silver, so a day's pay held less silver than before. Since goods were priced by silver and those prices barely changed, a day's wages bought less in 1560 than in 1540.
explanation.A: Correct. Twice as many coins, each with less than half the silver, means less silver per day; with silver prices steady, that buys less.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This takes the doubled wage at face value, ignoring that each coin contained less than half its former silver.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says laborers were paid in silver coins and never mentions payment in gold.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Lindqvist's data cover building laborers in the capital only, so they cannot show how their pay compared with that of all other workers.
